title: Drangleic
snippet: Centuries after the end of Vendrick's reign, Drangleic would be known in Lothric as "Drang", the land of the legend of the Linking of the Fire. Vendrick's name has been lost to history, who is remembered only as the "Old King of Want", an ancient ruler that was cursed by an all-consuming thirst, making him no king at all in the end. The Dragonriders of his royal guard and their immense strength are also properly remembered. A group of soldiers, who proclaimed themselves descendants of Drangleic and wore the geisteel armor made by the blacksmith of Vendrick's Castle, abandoned the region and became sellswords. Known as Drang Knights, they scattered across the lands and quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive fighting tactics that utilized twinspears and hammers, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies.

title: Drangleic
snippet: As the King of Drangleic, Vendrick proved himself a fair and just monarch, and expected similar behavior from his subjects, whom he trusted and rewarded according to their loyalty and deeds. Drangleic prospered and became an influential nation to the point of making Vendrick known as "the one that ruled over the world of man" Having obtained total political dominion over the lands of Drangleic, he left extant religious institutions and their traditions intact. The king had a lukewarm opinion of their holy powers, and clerics were kept at a distance from the royal court, their inherited roles relegated to ceremonial positions, without opportunities for attaining greater power.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Thanks to this discovery Vendrick became the monarch who came closest to becoming a true "King" and turning his wants into reality. He had access to the primordial Flame whose power could decide the fate of the world, either by linking it to prolong the state of the world or refusing this fate and leading the world to darkness as a Dark Lord. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. Nashandra helped bring peace to the kingdom, a peace so profound that it reminded humans of the Dark from which they came.

title: Drangleic

In the meantime, the soldiers of Vendrick defending their fortress died and eventually became hollows, though they continued to defend their country with honor, patrolling the area. Even with the Giants eventually defeated, victory had come all too late. Without a king, an exhausted army and with a country reduced to rubble, depopulated and infested with hollows, the kingdom of Drangleic fell apart. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

Those who could afford it ran away to other countries while the poor were left without a place to sleep, the kingdom now reduced to ruins. The conflict continued for three generations unabated, with the Giants sustaining their attacks on northern fortifications and trying to push their way inland towards the Royal Castle. The bodies of the many dead giants that littered the region slowly grew into great trees, covering the area around Cardinal Tower in a dense forest.

As a frontline commander, Vendrick favored simple, honest warriors who relied only on their own brute strength; as such, his army avoided dependence on sorceries or miracles, valuing physical ability alone. Before they could aspire to ride wyrms, Vendrick's warriors had to learn to wield great bows that required inhuman strength just to merely draw and great skill to shoot. After his kingdom was invaded by King Vendrick, who was under the influence of Nashandra, the Giant Lord invaded Drangleic to avenge his losses, and to retrieve the prize that Vendrick stole from him. More and more desperate, Vendrick came to call into his kingdom even mad warriors almost resembling beasts, that came from well beyond his borders and unknown lands.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick organized his army under simple ranks like Royal Guards, Knights, Soldiers and Infantry. He valued his royal army greatly, and included in its ranks even mere infantry, equipping each royal soldier with high-quality equipment crafted by the royal blacksmiths and armor with a design inspired by a brave knight from an old legend. The stalwart soldiers of Vendrick did not abandon their posts even as they became hollows, guarding their stations without relent. Distinguished soldiers were rewarded with magical rings that empowered them to carry more equipment, as proof of their meritorious deeds. Velstadt and Raime, two distinguished knights, became the left and right arms of Vendrick. Raime was enticed by the strength of his lord and acknowledged him as a father figure, while Velstadt was lured into Drangleic from a faraway home and devoted himself in life and death to his lord, eventually forgetting why he even came to the realm. Velstadt also became the leader of the elite

title: Olaphis
snippet: The kingdom of Olaphis soon fell to the curse, most of its population turned undead or hollow and others perished in the mad purges of the king. Traces of Olaphis culture remained in the region through history. The "Lost" Bastille became the stronghold of the kingdom of Venn, where the Belfry Luna of the princess was built and defended by Belfry Gargoyles, while the Kingdom of Alken was able to recover the Flame Swathe pyromancy of Straid. Some of the wise men who survived the purges of the king and the desperate sea voyage, reaching the south, imparted their knowledge of sorcery and pyromancy to the land where they ended up. Olenford in particular became revered as the father of sorcery in the country that they would help found and that would become known by the name of Melfia. Much later King Vendrick and his brother Aldia conducted research on Olaphis, managing to rediscover Straid's sorceries like Soul Bolt.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet:
Although Drummond and his forces fought valiantly against their foes, the war of attrition had left the armies of Drangleic crippled. They were simply no match for the Giants, fueled by a singular rage against Vendrick and his sins. Despite the captain's fielty to the kingdom, he too believed the king's barbarism to have been misguided, and he saw greater intellect in the actions of his foes, despite their seemingly barbaric appearance and disposition.

While his men were on the brink of defeat, he still wished to topple the leader of the invading Giants no matter the cost, knowing it would surely bring an end to the conflict. It is then that he met with a mysterious hero not from around those parts: the Bearer of the Curse, who had traveled back in time with the Ancient Dragon's gift. Together, they can team up against the Giant Lord and dispell the invading army for good, signaling the end of the generational war, though it came all to late and most of the kingdom was already lost.

title: Human Effigy

title: Drangleic
snippet: In the darkest hour of his reign, Vendrick also realized that his Queen, Nashandra, was a creature of the Abyss, and harbored an insatiable desire for strength. She was a fragment of a dark creature taken a human form, obsessed with the King's powerful soul. Impelled by her cravings, Nashandra sought souls, and strove to make the strength of the Giants her own, everything to reach the Throne of Want and the link for the First Flame so it could spread the Dark. Her painting in the castle was in fact able to curse the undead, making them hollow and draining their life, and only the king knew whether the depiction of the Queen was a resentful mockery, or an affectionate exaltation. At this point Vendrick had achieved a profound understanding of the truths of the world. He understood how the fire of souls was not enough to harness the curse, and how the Flame would soon fade and the souls of ancient beings would reemerge, before Dark would descend as a curse on humans, making them take

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

title: Knight King Rendal
snippet:
Knight King Rendal -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Rendal was the legendary "Knight King" of his homeland Balder. He wore a special ring capable of granting its wearer with the protection of iron, leading many legends to circulate about him. One of them claimed that not even the claws of a gigantic wyvern would be able to damage it. Silver Coins were even minted portraying his face, similarly to those of the gods McLoyf and Allfather Lloyd, which denoted his importance to mankind.

However, with the fading of the First Flame, more and more Undead started to appear among humans to the point that Balder was overrun by them, which caused the kingdom to be reduced to ruins in the ensuing chaos. Because of this, the Knight King gathered the remaining Balder Knights of his country and left for Lordran, the ancient kingdom of the gods. According to a legend, the Undead would make pilgrimage and overcome various trials to learn about their fate.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Studying and experimenting on the inhuman creatures and their souls, and via studies on artifacts from older kingdoms, Vendrick and Aldia pioneered the creation of Golems, very similar in appearance to the captured giants. Vendrick made Nashandra his queen, and had the golems build his Royal Castle, as proof of his gratitude and affection to her. Beneath the royal castle was the ancient Throne of Want, an artifact capable of connecting to the First Flame, the source of souls and beginning of all that the king was seeking. Studying the First Flame and the mysteries of the soul with his brother Aldia, the king acquired a profound understanding of the history of the world and the rules of reality, how the Flame brought Disparity and everything from it, propagating souls in the world every time someone linked it, giving it new strength. He also understood how the Dark was kept under control as long as the fire flourished, and that once the fire naturally weakened the curse would strike

title: Drangleic

title: Dragonrider
snippet:
Dragonrider -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Dragonriders used to serve in King Vendrick's royal guard long ago. These riders mounted wyverns and caused chaos on the battlefield due to their unparalleled strength. The rank of Dragonrider was reserved for honorable warriors who helped found Drangleic. Together with the King, they crushed the land's former inhabitants and erected a magnificent kingdom upon their graves.

Those wishing to join the ranks of the Dragonriders were forced to undergo intense and dangerous training. Only those who passed the training were allowed in the order, those who failed would be ripped apart by the very mounts they tried to command.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : Vendrick is initially passive, and will aggro only upon taking enough damage from the player. This is affected by the number of Giant Souls in the player's possession, so attacking him in his initial encounter after the battle with Velstadt will not aggro him.
By using a Bonfire Ascetic at the Undead Ditch bonfire, Vendrick can be respawned, but so will Velstadt.
If Vendrick is killed before going and slaying Nashandra, the player will have to fight Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin, which can ultimately cause Aldia to be the third boss in a row, assuming the Throne Watcher and Defender are not yet defeated.
If a player summoned for the Velstadt fight has any Souls of a Giant in their possession they will reduce Vendrick's defense immediately after the fight. If the area is abandoned or the player dies in that first fight he will reset and only calculate the player's Giant Souls.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: The king married the future Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric, with whom he conceived the divine princes of the kingdom.Lorian, the crown prince, received the ancient brass armor handed down by the royal family, complete with a crown patterned with flame, symbolic of the kingdom's tradition of Firelinking. Lorian was raised as a knight and proved his incredible prowess on the battlefield, leading a war against the remnants of the Chaos Demons, even capturing some of them to serve the kingdom as slaves. Lorian went on to face the Demon Prince, defeating him single-handedly in a battle that eternally scorched his greatsword with the flame of chaos and stained his armor black.

title: New Londo Ruins

title: The Nameless King
snippet: The Falconers, a group of mercenaries hired to protect the elites of Volgen, were still part of the covenant of those that worshipped the God of the Sun and possessed their Sunlight Medals. Moreover, in Lindelt, a "sacred land" known for its clerics and miracles, the Nameless King's miracles of Lightning Spear and Great Lightning Spear were preserved and passed down within its religion, although the names of the clan of gods and the sun god had been lost. Furthermore, some other miracles of the god such as the Sunlight Blade and the Sacred Oath appear to have been part of the lost culture of Olaphis, indicating a continuing tradition of the cult of the Nameless King, even if fragmentary, throughout the history of Drangleic.

snippet:
Velstadt, the Royal Aegis -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Originating from a foreign land, Velstadt was King Vendrick's right-hand man, along with Raime, and one of his most loyal knights as well as the Commander of his forces. At some point, Velstadt and Raime quarreled, ending with Raime being declared a traitor and leaving the King's service. Velstadt would always be by his king's side and followed him to the Undead Crypt when he fled Drangleic Castle. Despite Vendrick's hollowed state, Velstadt remains, protecting his liege and serving as the king's last line of defense.

Given he, or rather a copy, can be summoned by Elana, the Squalid Queen, he may have a connection to Shulva.

title: Old Iron King
snippet: The Iron King was later approached by Sir Alonne, a great warrior from the east, who trained the King's soldiers and helped him forge a kingdom for himself from the old Kingdom of Venn. Doing so cost the Iron King what little resources he had, but in the process, he discovered an iron-producing miracle, which allowed him to freely shape and harness the powers of iron. With this new power, the Old Iron King became extremely wealthy and powerful, forging from iron both his entire castle, and various golems such as the Ironclads and the Smelter Demons. The King also entertained various craftsmen and savants from many lands, most of whom were charlatans, but many still brought innovations for his kingdom, such as the artisan who crafted the weapon of his Alonne Knigths and Magus Eygil, a pyromancer who wanted to breath life into fire. He was known for cershing rings that bore the protection of dragons throughout all of his life and service to Drangleic. He might have been an exceptional champion, however, as the first of his rings is the second highest reward of the Company of Champions covenant, a group of brave warriors based in Majula who scoff at danger and seek greater challenges, their names engraved to commemorate their deeds.

snippet:
Looking Glass Knight -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore

Before the King's fall and the collapse of his kingdom, the knight would serve as a test to warriors who wished to serve under the king. After Vendrick went into hiding in the Undead Crypt, the knight from then on served as the first line of defense against those attempting to pursue the now hollowed king. It continues to challenge individuals who cross its path.

title: Drangleic
snippet:
Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - location - description

Far in the north of Drangleic, beyond the great sea, there is an unexplored continent where the race of the giants lives. To the east, Drangleic borders with the kingdom of Mirrah while in the distant east the land of Jugo and the ruins of the kingdom of Forossa are located. To the northeast, Drangleic borders with the frozen ruins of the kingdom of Eleum Loyce. To the west, Drangleic borders with the city of Volgen. To the south, Drangleic borders with the kingdom of Melfia while in the distant south the land of Lanafir is located.

snippet:

This passage once served as the final test awaiting those who wished to serve in Vendrick's royal guard, by testing their might against the Looking Glass Knight.

Now, this desolate and decrepit part of the castle serves as the home for the Looking Glass Knight, who to this day awaits worthy foes and defends the road to the Shrine, ensuring only the worthy may pass.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Faraam is the name that the people of Forossa used in veneration of Gwyn's firstborn after his name was lost over the centuries. The Lion Knights of Forossa, besides bearing the title "Lion" same as Gwyn's firstborn and first knight, were not only mighty but rabid warriors obsessed with fighting; Forossan knights knew only war and no other ways of living, to the point that they didn't even know what they were fighting for, similarly to the Nameless King who "had respect only for arms, and nothing else".

title: Mirrah
snippet: Towards the end of his reign, Vendrick hired some of the deserting Shadow Knights from Mirrah to fight against the hollows in an attempt to stave off the curse that was plaguing his kingdom. He put them to work in the No-man's Wharf where they sent the imprisoned undead to die in the sea, but before long they became hollow themselves.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
At a certain moment during his reign, Nashandra came to Drangleic, she coveted the Throne of Want and the power of the First Flame, and seduced Vendrick in order to use him as a means to accomplish her goal, becoming his queen.

Much time later, after Drangleic was ravaged due to both the war with the Giants and the undead curse, which all of Vendrick’s and Aldia’s plans to cure were in vain, Vendrick found out about Nashandra's plan: to use the throne to claim the First Flame for herself. Vendrick reacted quickly and sent the Throne Watcher and the Throne Defender to guard the throne. He then fled to the Undead Crypt, where he eventually went Hollow, to keep his ring and soul from the wrong hands. He did all this in an attempt to stop Nashandra.

title: Old Ones
snippet:
Old Ones -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Despite Wellager claims, it's impossible for Vendrick to have defeated "the Old Ones of his time"
** The Old Iron King predates Vendrick's rule by many years, and he's still in possession of Gwyn's soul in the present.
** If the Lost Sinner and the Rotten are respectively the princess of Venn and the Sunken King, they too are much older than Vendrick.

title: Lindelt
snippet: Thanks to their well-honed miracles and unwavering faith in the face of death, the cleric knights of the Archdrake Church were a formidable force on the battlefield, even managing to stand up to the army of King Vendrick as worthy rivals. Miracles like Replenishment and Resplendent Life allowed the knights to endure and heal from arduous battles. Among the high-ranked clerics, Forsalle stood out thanks to his mastery of miracles, and led many battles across his country's borders. He earned the title of "holy knight" and was feared for his "demonic power" by his enemies. However, some cleric knights of Lindelt defected to escape their country's authoritarian rule. These clerics tried to start new lives in the destroyed kingdom of Drangleic and found their way inside the Shrine of Amana, where some of them went hollow.

title: Felkin the Outcast
snippet:
Eventually, Felkin's research into hexes and the Dark brought him to the fallen kingdom of Drangleic, "where Dark runs deeper than anywhere else", likely due to the Throne of Want holding the power of the fading First Flame and making the kingdom the epicenter of the Undead curse and a potential coming of an Age of Dark.

It is of note that, having come to Drangleic to research the Dark and not in search of a cure for Undeath, Felkin explicitly states that he is not undead, making him one of the very few uncursed humans in the kingdom. Felkin has a stutter of sorts, although it is unclear if it is an actual speech disorder or merely his tendency to get lost in his own thoughts of the Dark.

According to legend, the Dragonriders straddled not horses, but wyrms.

Aspiring Dragonriders who had not the mettle to handle their training were torn apart by the wyrms, and those who survived emerged with deific strength.

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet: Rumors abound in Drangleic about the king's brother, Lord Aldia, who tried to create a dragon. Perhaps the existence of the Ancient Dragon, and its dubious origins, are testament to his success.

title: The Old Chaos
snippet: The king made some attempts to combat the Chaos, and his knights delved valiantly into the depths to exterminate the terrible things that dwelled there, but not one of them returned. Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce. He traveled deep into the Chaos with his knights until he was devoured by the flames.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
She eventually finds this someone in the Bearer of the Curse, an undead with no memory of their origins from a far away land. Shanalotte guides the Bearer of the Curse in their quest, telling them to seek souls and to seek the king. She will guide the Bearer of the Curse to seek out the Four Old Ones in order to claim their powerful souls. Once the Bearer of the Curse has done this, the way to Drangleic Castle, the home of Vendrick, will be open. Shanalotte will wait outside the castle, directing the Bearer of the Curse to enter.

She will next appear in the Undead Crypt, where Vendrick now wanders aimlessly. After the Bearer of the Curse has claimed the king's ring, she will direct them to follow the mark of the king and journey east, and warn them that if they continue on this path, they too will one day walk these same grounds, without really knowing why.

title: New Londo Ruins

 dark_souls_ii : Although the Four Kings had been defeated, the seal that contained the ruins of New Londo and the water that had submerged it had been removed and as a result the remaining Darkwraiths were free to spread across the rest of the world, continuing to wreak havoc. Although these knights subsumed by dark never reached Drangleic in strength, knowledge of their existence has come to the region through foreign legends as poor souls who chased the art of Lifedrain and were able to freely manipulate the Dark, implying that they attacked the countries around Drangleic.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Balder
snippet: However, with the fading of the First Flame, more and more Undead started to appear among humans, to the point that in Balder it reached a widespread outbreak and the kingdom was reduced to ruins in the ensuing chaos. Knight King Rendal thus gathered the remaining knights of his country and left for Lordran, the ancient kingdom of the gods where according to legend the Undead would have to pilgrimage and overcome various tests to learn about their fate. In an attempt to reach Anor Londo to link the fading Flame and thus save what remained of their kingdom, nullifying the Curse of Undeath, Rendal and his knights arrived at the Sen's Fortress which tested the potential Chosen Undead with deadly challenges. title: Forossa
snippet: The highest ranking knight of Forossa, together with Forossan sages and knights, abandoned his home and moved to the northeast of Drangleic before reaching a land that was plagued by a fragment of the Bed of Chaos. This offshoot of the Flame of Chaos, seedbed of the Demons, had been spawning monsters and atrocities in the region, whose residents were forced into flight. The knight saw the suffering of the population and devoted himself to the protection of their land. And so he acceded to the throne as the Ivory King, and battled the raging Chaos, empowered by his great soul. He governed as a true and ever-merciful monarch in the kingdom he built, dedicating himself to protecting his land and being the first to swing his sword in times of need. The country existed to contain the Chaos and the terrors it generated, and its knights became the devoted guardians of the land, delving valiantly into its depths, knowing that they may never return.

title: Chancellor Wellager
snippet:
Chancellor Wellager -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : Wellager claims Vendrick defeated the Old Ones to build Drangleic, but the claim is quite dubious, as they are present when the Bearer of the Curse starts their adventure. This is either an outdated line of dialogue that reflects an earlier version of the plot, or implies there were different Old Ones when Vendrick founded Drangleic.
His model is actually completely textured, but it never shows up like that in-game through normal means due to his ghostly filter, a trait he shares with the Wall Warrior enemy.
Although he is transparent, messages can't be seen through him.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world had become irreparably corrupted, and all lands from all previous points in time had begun to converge upon a single point: the Kingdom of Lothric. Upon reviving and seeing what had become of the world they had fought to protect, the Lords of Cinder, too, rejected the linking of the Flame and refused to sit upon their thrones. Aldrich, one of the Lords of Cinder, decided not to take his throne after experiencing visions of the deep sea and its inevitable coming.

snippet:
Royal Guard -  Dark Souls II - enemy - lore 
 lore : High ranking soldiers in Vendrick's army, these knights were gifted weapons and equipment modeled on Sir Syan, one of Drangleic's military leaders. However Sir Syan was killed during the war against the Giants and his armor became cursed. Shortly after his death, the unfortunate knights that wore his armor were driven insane.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them was Aldrich who, like the other exhumed Lords, had no intention of sacrificing himself again, as his reflections on the state of the world had led him to understand that an Age of the Deep would soon arrive, motivating him to devour the gods themselves, in order to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep led by Archdeacon McDonnell, Aldrich would march on Irithyll, intent on capturing Anor Londo to devour the king of the gods himself. However, he would find his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White so easily. From the ensuing battle Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and defeating

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Centuries after Gwyn sacrificed his soul to link the Flame, some remnants of it manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region. At some point the Old Iron King came into contact with the soul of Gwyn, which had become "Ichorous Earth" and produced the scorching iron and magma of the Iron Keep. The Old Iron King was thus destroyed by the mass of iron possessed by the soul of Gwyn who then went on to control the remains of the Old Iron King, creating a demonic-looking creature made of melted iron.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Azal, Sage of Forossa
snippet:
Azal, Sage of Forossa -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Azal was an accomplished sage of Forossa, one of the Northwarders who earn their title after surviving a journey of great hardship. He was exceptionally skilled as he imbued his staff with magic, granting it unique powers. This made the tool unwieldy for the inexperienced, which proved the sage's magical prowess.

What became of him is unknown, but his staff can be retrieved on a corpse in Eleum Loyce, a kingdom ruled by a Forossan champion. It's possible, then, that Azal died in the frozen city, perhaps while investigating what had happened to it.

title: Olaphis
snippet:
Olaphis -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : Olaphis was a kingdom that once stood on the land which corresponds to the domains of Drangleic under the reign of King Vendrick. The country was one of many kingdoms that rose and fell throughout the history of the region. The immense fortress of the Bastille was the residence of the country's ruler and the nucleus of the kingdom, its land extending as far as the regions that would be later known as Brightstone Cove Tseldora and the Shrine of Amana.

Olaphis was a sophisticated society home to advanced technology and magic, developed in both sorceries and pyromancies. Its craftsmen were credited with complex designs, known for their refined halberds and powerful staves. The kingdom seems to have mined the brightstone in their territories and turned them into crystals, which were used in their catalysts to amplify sorceries.

title: Mad Knight of Alken
snippet:
Mad Knight of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Not much is known about Adgars, other than the fact he belonged to the kingdom of Alken and that he was considered mad. He wielded a peculiar weapon, which is what the Rings of Blades are modeled after. In the era of Drangleic they are associated with the Pursuer, a mysterious accursed knight who holds onto them.

title: Chancellor Wellager
snippet:
Chancellor Wellager -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Chancellor Wellager was one of Vendrick's most important servants, having been present for all of his greatest accomplishments; the founding of the kingdom of Drangleic, the arrival of his queen Nashandra, the construction of the castle and the invasion of the land of Giants, which resulted in the creation of the Golems. This led to a period of peace that the advisor described to be akin to the Dark, a hint to the queen's true nature.

His king had once ordered him to enlist the great blacksmith Llewellyn from the land of Mirrah with a lifetime contract, so that the kingdom of Drangleic could have access of the rare geisteel from the eastern land, which had been secret until then. Wellager would succeed in this, even being gifted the Espada Ropera by the blacksmith. His exploits would strengthen the kingdom greatly.

Balder was the home of the Knight King Rendal, but the kingdom was reduced to ruins after a widespread outbreak of Undead.

title: Priest's Chime
snippet:
Priest's Chime -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Sacred chime granted to high-ranking clerics. A catalyst for miracles and hexes.

Drangleic was the home of many clerics, but King Vendrick held a lukewarm opinion of their powers, and kept them only as attendants to ceremony. In this sense, Drangleic was not the place for a cleric with any ambition.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa was also the origin of the special and powerful black firebombs capable of causing large flames and explosions. These bombs, due to the risk they posed to their owners, were subject to strict standards for their safe storage, codified in the kingdom's legislature.

Forossa eventually fell to war, its military and government exhausted to the point of collapse. The fall of the country left its citizens to their own devices, most of whom became bandits and thieves that infested the outskirts of their fallen home, or scattered across the continent. Without an element of cohesion, the remaining Forossan knights became mercenaries, selling their fighting strength to foreign armies. Among these Lion Knight mercenaries was Vengarl of Forossa, once a ferocious warrior on the battlefield, who came to Drangleic and served under the command of King Vendrick.

title: Velka, Goddess of Sin
snippet:
Velka, Goddess of Sin -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : At some point, Velka's influence and her followers reached Drangleic, who began creating magical rings with the shape of crow claws around a gem attuned with different elements, artifacts that remain in the region even centuries after the collapse of Vendrick's kingdom.

In Tseldora a church was built venerating the dark goddess, depicted with her iconic Book of the Guilty and talisman. Above the building Cromwell can also be found, a man who wears the robes of her ancient pardoners and performs the ritual function of absolving humans of their sins, offering forgiveness to anyone as long as they are sincere.

Despite the presence of pardoners like Cromwell, the very name Velka was lost to time in Drangleic, even as the pardoner outfit continued to serve its intended purpose; albeit under the mere shadow of the authority it represented, not the forgotten Goddess of Sin herself who was once feared by many.

title: Melfia
snippet: Melfia was founded by several sorcerers from the region of Drangleic, in particular from the lost kingdom of Olaphis. The king of Olaphis, with his kingdom plagued by the curse of undeath, grew paranoid as to the source of the curse. In a foolish attempt to keep them out of sight, the king rounded up the undead and locked them in droves inside the Bastille. Those perceived as a threat by the king were seized, cursed or no, and impounded in the prison fortress. Sorcerers in particular suffered dreadful persecution; the famed Straid of Olaphis was among those imprisoned. As the Bastille was saturated with undead, the king of Olaphis used the Flexile Sentry golems to cram them into crude ships and sent them to the sea, condemned to certain death. Many sank with the ships, however a small number of survivors drifted to the south and settled down. Among them were several sorcerers who imparted their knowledge to the new land where they ended up. Olenford in particular became revered as the

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - dragonslaying_foundation 
 dragonslaying_foundation : The origins of the kingdom of Lothric can be traced to the legacy of Drangleic. Survivors of Forossa and Vendrick's Kingdom, together with followers of the Way of Blue and the Heirs of the Sun, were the first inhabitants of Lothric, bringing with them artifacts such as the Spirit Tree and Golden Wing Crest Shields, the Sunlight Straight Sword and even the same Priest's Chimes to their new home.

title: Shrine of Amana
snippet:
Shrine of Amana -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : The shrine was once dedicated to sustaining the Demon of Song, long before the undead curse ravaged the kingdom of Drangleic.

title: Princess of Venn
snippet:
Princess of Venn -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : The Princess of Venn was the heir to the throne of her kingdom. Her homeland despised the neighboring kingdom of Alken, and this feud was kept alive by both countries. Yet in spite of such deep-seated hatred, the young royal fell in love with the prince of the enemy kingdom, who himself felt the same way. Theirs was a forbidden love.

title: Gods
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.
King Oceiros, the King of Lothric who married Gwynevere. It is unknown what his original species was, but he would later become similar to a hybrid in an attempt to turn into a Dragon. He is the father of at least three of Gwynevere's children: Lorian, Lothric (named after the kingdom) and her youngest, Ocelotte, none of whom were deified; it is unclear whether or not he fathered Rosaria, the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, or Gertrude, but as Lorian was the heir to the throne, he was likely the two's oldest son, and perhaps their oldest child together.

title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The story of *Dark Souls II* is not directly connected to *Dark Souls*, though they are set in the same world.

The game takes place in Drangleic, a once prosperous land under the rule of King Vendrick, which has fallen to ruin throughout the ages with the raging war between humans and giants, the sudden disappearance of the King, and the spreading of the Undead Curse. Like many others, the protagonist has come to the crumbling kingdom in search of a cure for their crippling affliction, the Curse of the Undead.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldia is the elder brother of King Vendrick, and aided his brother in founding the kingdom of Drangleic. He secluded himself in his manor, searching for secrets of life, viewing the Undead as the key to finding it. For his reverence of the Undead, Aldia was shunned by Vendrick, banished to his Keep forever. People who were invited to his manor commonly disappeared and were replaced with malformed beasts. The Southern and Northern Ritual Bands were created by Aldia and his acolytes after cruel, horrible experiments were performed on these people. Many valuable objects came out of Aldia's Keep, including the Sunset Staff, the Spitfire Spear, Soul Geyser, Unleash Magic, and Forbidden Sun.

Through his experiments, Aldia sought to learn the nature of the undead curse, and to shed the yoke of fate. He failed, however, and turned into a monstrosity, inhabiting the bonfires.

title: Llewellyn
snippet:
Llewellyn -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the age of the kingdom of Lothric, Llewellyn's legacy seems to have lived on, as his name, occupation and geisteel work survive in the Llewellyn Shield, currently found in the possession of Horace the Hushed. More of his equipment found its way into this new age, though it became associated with the Drang Knights instead, mercenaries who descended from the inhabitants of the vanished kingdom of Drangleic. Since their armors were given only to selected members of the castle, it's likely that they are descended from Vendrick's court.

title: Alonne Knight

Alonne Knight -  Dark Souls II - enemy - lore

The Knights of Alonne were loyal servants of the Old Iron King who were tasked with defending his fortress from intruders. Even after the castle was swallowed by lava and the king was transformed into a demon, the knights continued to serve their master and protect the ruins of his kingdom.

title: Llewellyn
snippet:
Llewellyn -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Llewellyn was a skilled blacksmith that hailed from the land of Mirrah, known for his pragmatic philosophy of simplicity over ostentation, leading to modest-looking yet extremely strong equipment. He was contracted by Chancellor Wellager by the orders of King Vendrick, who wished to introduce the rare geisteel alloy to the armies of Drangleic. The master smith was so pleasd by his offer that he gifted the chancellor with one of his works, the Espada Ropera, when he moved from his homeland to that of his contractors.

Geisteel would soon find itself on some of the weapons of Drangleic's most renowned knights, though they were seldom used in combat due to the rarity of the alloy, even with Llewellyn living in the castle. Special armors were also crafted by the master smith, given only to a select few members of Drangleic's court, which included Wellager himself.

title: Santier
snippet:
Santier -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Santier was a large living statue, capable of movement, meaning it was likely a golem of some kind, which the country of Drangleic was known to manufacture.

According to a legend in the kingdom, the statue was defeated using a spear, which is now hidden in the Doors of Pharros and guarded by the followers of the Rat King. All that remains of Santier is its head, stuck to the very spear that ended it, hindering the weapon's effectiveness until even that last remnant is smashed to pieces.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet:
Champion Gundyr -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that Gundyr was an ancient king of Lothric, or was given an armor modeled after that of a king of Lothric and thus served as their champion. This is because the story of his tragic failure to link the Flame became a legend among the local population and the kingdom of Lothric was deeply linked to the tradition of Firelinking, so much so that Gundyr's arena was located right next to the city and close to Firelink Shrine. Gundyr's failure and the resulting stain on the king's reputation would also explain the desperation of future rulers of the kingdom, which culminated in Oceiros's obsession with producing a Lord of Cinder of royal blood.

title: Mirrah
snippet: The excellent alloy called "geisteel" had also been invented in the country of Mirrah, and never sold abroad. The rare material allowed the crafting of equipment that offered top-notch protection at a very light weight. As such, its method of manufacture was kept secret from foreign lands, since it provided the kingdom's army with an innovative edge over its enemies. The secrets of geisteel were exported when King Vendrick ordered Chancellor Wellager to hire a craftsman of geisteel. Wellager managed to bring the craftsman Llewellyn back to Drangleic with him. Allocated a blinding salary, Llewellyn became the castle's resident master smith and began working for Vendrick, forging geisteel armor along with long daggers and shields, and distinguished himself for his lack of ostentation and focus on simplicity and strength. His smithy supplied only a select few, including the chancellor himself and the Stone Soldiers and Stone Knights.

title: Ironclad Soldier
snippet:
Ironclad Soldier -  Dark Souls II - enemy - lore 
 lore : The Ironclad Soldiers were created by the Old Iron King and brought to life by an "enchantment of souls", making these soldiers comparable to the golems of Vendrick and the Ivory King.

At some point, warriors wearing decrepit armor emerged from Drangleic Castle, and quietly assumed positions amongst the royal army. This implies that Vendrick was able to obtain the means to control or create these mighty warriors. They never spoke a word nor showed their faces, likely due to their souls being embedded into the armor itself, rather than a creature within.

title: Ocelotte
snippet: Once his desire for transcendence was satiated, Oceiros once again fathered a child with Gwynevere, believing that a descendant of dragons would make a worthy Champion. Either because of the child was born deformed and monstrous, or because she suffered violence from Oceiros or was horrified by the King's decaying sanity, but the birth of Ocelotte was too much for the Queen Gwynevere to bare: she decided to abandon the kingdom never to return again, leaving the newborn with the twisted father. Once he obtained Ocelotte, Oceiros retreated with his royal guard to the gardens close to the Firelink Shrine, completely ignoring the state of his kingdom to protect the "child of dragons" who represented the culmination of his desires and the only thing left in his life. Despite everything, the king was not even able to see Ocelotte, holding him tightly in his palm and relying only on his madness.

title: Smelter Demon
snippet: The Smelter Demon found in the Iron Keep was responsible for the death of the Old Iron King, and by extension the full fall of his kingdom. Although his existence as the man he was before ended, the King became a golem-like being himself, possessed by an incredibly powerful soul that lurked below the magma.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: With the threat of Chaos temporarily contained the Ivory King was able to build his kingdom and he governed it as a true and ever-merciful monarch, dedicating himself to protecting his land and being the first to swing his sword in times of need. He curiously kept his countenance from his people and his Knights dutifully followed suit, never unhinging their helmets in public view. The kingdom of Eleum Loyce continued to exist with the aim of containing the Chaos and the terrors it generated and its knights became the devoted guardians of the land, delving valiantly into the depths even if that meant never to return. The Ivory King, who came into contact with the magical arts of the nearby Drangleic, also built Rampart Golems and granted them life, charging them with the containment of the creatures of Chaos within the boundaries of the wall.  description : Straid was a sworn brother-in-arms of the ancient king of old Olaphis. Together, they slew the Ancient Dragon, and tasted of omniscience.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa -  Dark Souls III - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the region and times of Lothric, Forossa was recognized as a kingdom that had been destroyed, but legends about its Lion Knights and those among them that became part of history remained alive.

Following the collapse of Forossa, its survivors, along with other groups originating from Drangleic, contributed to founding the kingdom of Lothric. One of the armor sets that were named for the ancient god of war worshipped by the Forossans was preserved; among the royal guard of Lothric is Lion Knight Albert, descendant of the order of Forossa Knights.

The brigands who survived the fall of Forossa, though no longer identified by their homeland, still roam the world wielding their ancient war axes.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : Forossa is a land located to the distant east of Drangleic.

The kingdom of Forossa was defined by war, constantly in conflict with its neighbors. Leading up to the fall of the nation, it was engaged in a protracted war with its neighbors. The culture and organization of the Forossan army rightly recognized and rewarded their soldiers for their strength, determination and diligence on the battlefield; those who distinguished themselves could, in the course of their lives, ascend from mere peasants to generals.

title: Old Ones
snippet: The four current owners of the Great Souls as of the Bearer of the Curse’s arrival in Drangleic are the Old Iron King, the Lost Sinner, The Rotten and The Duke's Dear Freja. The Emerald Herald instructs the Bearer of the Curse to acquire the Great Souls to gain their power and use them as a beacon to reach Vendrick.

title: Aava, the King's Pet
snippet:
Aava, the King's Pet -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : ***Swipe:** Aava swipes at the player with a paw from the side. May be followed by a second swipe with the other paw.
***Backwards Leap:** Aava leaps backwards, dodging player attacks, and damages & knocks down anyone it lands upon.

title: Aava, the King's Pet
snippet:
Aava, the King's Pet -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Aava is a challenging opponent as it is highly agile and capable of dealing huge amounts of damage. She also corrodes your weapon(s), making them degrade far faster than normal, a slightly weaker version of Sinh.

On top of dealing high damage, most of the attacks are difficult to block. As such, it's often a good idea to take focus on evading the attacks as turtling often results in the player's guard being broken, which is often fatal.

Aava is very evasive, and will often keep a distance between itself and the player when not attacking. However, Aava can use the distance to give the player a false sense of security, as it can close the distance in the blink of an eye, surprising unaware players. This means that the player must make the most of the openings given, as they're unable to safely otherwise. This is especially true if they're unable to utilize ranged attacks.

title: Aava, the King's Pet
snippet:
Aava, the King's Pet -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : Approaching the fog wall for the first time, a voice warns: *"Go back. Aava is watching"*. After entering the mist, the voice speak again: *"Poor Aava, do you miss your king? The one without the sign has arrived. Do be merciful, and end things swiftly."* Aava is initially invisible and will attack the player in this form.

After progressing through the ruins of the city, the Eye of the Priestess can eventually be found at a glowing altar, which will reveal Aava and other invisible entities. After entering the fog gate again, the voice calls out: *"This dead city has nothing to offer. Go back. Do not seek the old Chaos, nor its twisted flame."* Continuing along the path to the cathedral, Aava can be seen sleeping above the entrance. Once close enough, Aava will jump down and the battle begins.

 notes : His moveset is similar to that of Old King Allant from *Demon's Souls*.
His armor, the Ivory King Set, can be purchased by Maughlin after getting 50 Loyce Souls.
If he gets close to one of the portals that spawns the Charred Loyce Knights while it is being frozen by one of the Knights, he will be instantly killed.
While attacking, he can be heard speaking. During most attacks he will yell out a hardly understandable "Fight!", or, more rarely, "Die!".

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
Burnt Ivory King -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : The player will not immediately face the Ivory King after passing through the fog door and dropping into the Old Chaos. Instead, the player will face three waves of Charred Loyce Knights who will emerge from the three portals around the arena. The knights will be a random mix of halberd, sword, or pyromancy users. During the first wave, three Knights will spawn. After a short period of time, several more will spawn, then several more shortly thereafter.

Finding the three uncorrupted Knights from around Eleum Loyce will be an immense help in the fight. Throughout the entire battle, the Knights will periodically freeze the portals, preventing Charred Knights from spawning.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
Burnt Ivory King -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Sword Buff**: Periodically throughout the fight, the King will take a few seconds to buff his sword with magic. Unlike the Smelter Demon, he does not have enhanced defenses during this period, which offers the chance to attack him with impunity.

**Ice Explosion**: Only used when the King has buffed his sword. He will slam the point into the ground, emitting a series of highly-damaging ice spikes in a circle around himself. Easily avoided by moving back from the King when he turns his sword upside down.

**Impale**: Only used with the buffed sword. Similar to Sir Alonne's impale attack, the King will charge up for a moment before lunging at the player. If he connects, he will lift the player on his sword, draining a large amount of health, after which he'll throw the player away.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
**Lunging Slash**: This attack will pass straight through shields when his sword is buffed, and is a danger because it will not knock the player down, opening the player up to his follow-up spin attack.

**Jumping Spin**: The King will jump into the air, spinning 360 degrees before slashing with his sword. He often uses this after his lunging slash.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
At an unknown point, an ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land. Legend holds that the Ivory King used his magnificent soul to build Eleum Loyce and contain the spread of Chaos. A grand cathedral was built in an attempt to appease the raging flame, but the Chaos would not be sated. As a precaution, various knights and golems were posted throughout the Garrison Ward to lead the advance on the swollen flame on his orders. Other knights were ordered to delve into the depths of Chaos to exterminate the terrible things that dwelt there, but not one of the knights returned.

Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. He traveled deep into the Chaos until he and his knights were corrupted by the flames. At some point after the King's departure, the ivory gates of the city were flung open, and the land grew cold and lifeless.

title: Crucifix of the Mad King
snippet:
Crucifix of the Mad King -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : One of the strongest and most unique weapons in the game, the Crucifix of the Mad King has many unique characteristics and can be extremely powerful when utilized properly.

As a halberd, the Crucifix possesses respectable range and a moderate swing speed on its attacks. It is a split-damage weapon, inflicting both physical and Dark damage with its attacks. This damage scales primarily with Strength and Faith, with Faith being the more important component as it governs both damage types. Along with its non-negligible Intelligence wielding requirement, this means that any build that wishes to use this weapon must be specifically tailored to use it.
